checklist.item: Secrets and server texts (tokens, header values, SMTP or upstream replies, file contents) in errors, logs and responses.
checklist.evidence: Validators: 17,620 hostile calls over 42 validator cases with a marker string as the value of every field (including secret, literal header values, {env} names, token secret): the marker never appears in an error. Only key names are repeated (unknown keys, header names; note N4). validateAdminCheckInput with a secret on an http check: 'check.secret: is only allowed on a heartbeat check', no value. fetchJson: the x-pulse-contract value appears in full in the wire-mismatch message and in http -> wire.error (4,014-character header -> 4,089-character error object as JSON; finding -4). Upstream body text appears in the invalid-json message (finding -5); an HTML body gives only "Unrecognized token '<'". On a network error, cause is the raw Bun error, whose path property holds the full URL with user info and query (JSON.stringify shows it, String does not; note N2). No logs and no responses in the library.

checklist.item: Authentication before any other check; status codes and their order on admin routes.
checklist.evidence: The library has no routes and authenticates nothing; the api enforces the order. The exported ADMIN_STATUS_ORDER is [404,401,403,413,400,428,503,412,422,409,404], the same as the docs/index.md table: 401 and 403 come before 413 and every other check; only the 'feature off' 404 is first.

checklist.item: Body and size limits on every method, also before any write.
checklist.evidence: fetchJson (GET only; no writes): a declared Content-Length of 100 MiB with 1 byte sent (raw TCP) -> too-large in 2 ms; endless chunked body -> too-large in 12 ms, RSS +13 MiB; maxBytes 1024 -> too-large in 1 ms; slow body with timeoutMs 1000 -> timeout in 1000 ms; a fetch that ignores the signal, timeoutMs 500 -> timeout in 501 ms. gzip/deflate responses decoding to 64 MiB..2 GiB: too-large, peak RSS +126..+178 MiB (bounded). Brotli/zstd responses of a few KiB: too-large only after peak RSS grows by about the decoded size (+1.3..+2.6 GiB; finding -1). maxBytes NaN or Infinity turns the cap off (note N3). Service constants ADMIN_MAX_BODY_BYTES 1,048,576 and TOKEN_MAX_BODY_BYTES 4,096 are enforced by the api; 413 precedes 400/422 in ADMIN_STATUS_ORDER. Validation of 5 MiB bodies: at most 279 ms (note N6).

checklist.item: Input validation at every trust boundary; validators never throw on any input type.
checklist.evidence: 17,620 calls over 42 cases (every exported validator) with 36 hostile values at the top level and at every field path to depth 5 (primitives, BigInt, Symbol, functions, classes, lone surrogate, NUL, 1 MB string, Date, RegExp, Map, typed array, null prototype, throwing and revoked Proxies, throwing-Proxy prototypes, throwing toPrimitive/toString/valueOf, throwing getters, symbol keys, cycles, nesting 100,000 deep, __proto__/constructor keys from JSON.parse, frozen objects): 0 throws, no prototype pollution. JSON nested 200,000 deep in jsonAssert.equals: rejected in 42 ms. Header rules hold for Host/HOST, a name with a space, LF or tab in a value, an {env} name with a newline, another prefix, lower case or Unicode. Finding -2: a header entry named __proto__ is never validated and pulse-probe then loads no checks.

checklist.item: No accessor or getter of untrusted input runs.
checklist.evidence: Every field of every valid sample replaced by a counting accessor: 0 runs. An accessor on a required field is rejected; on one of 31 optional fields it reads as absent and the result is ok:true with the same object returned, so a caller that reads the field later runs the getter (note N1; JSON.parse never creates accessors). Getters planted on Object.prototype run inside schema refinements (start, end, action, status, resolvedAt, count, p50Ms, p95Ms), and a numeric-index getter there makes 24 of the 42 validator cases reject valid input (finding -6; needs code already running in the process).

checklist.item: SSRF: allowed targets, environment lookups, redirects (cross-origin, https to http), forwarded headers.
checklist.evidence: Redirects: fetchJson follows 302 and 307 to another host name and port and from https to plain http, and returns the value read there (finding -3). Bun drops Authorization and Cookie on those hops; a custom credential header (x-api-key) reached the other origin and the plain-http host. notify wraps fetch with redirect: manual; probe and status do not. Allowed targets: check url must be http(s) without user info (8 user-info forms rejected); file: and javascript: rejected; loopback, private and link-local targets accepted by design, the target policy is in the probe (note N7). Environment lookups: src/ reads no environment (grep process.env|Bun.env: no hits); {env} names must match ^PULSE_HEADER_\w{1,115}$, which a __proto__ header entry skips, but the probe checks the prefix and host binding again (finding -2). Forwarded headers: not applicable, no server.
The library writes no files: src/ imports no node: module and has no fs, Bun.file or rename (grep: no hits). dist/ is a committed build output.

checklist.item: Dependencies, Docker base images and CI actions pinned and approved (docs/approved-packages.md).
checklist.evidence: Runtime: zod 4.6.7, exact, approved, sha512 integrity in bun.lock; bun install --frozen-lockfile --production installs only zod. Dev: @biomejs/biome 2.6.3, lefthook 2.2.2, @types/node 26.6.6, @types/bun 1.4.0, typescript7 npm:typescript@7.0.2, pulse-config by full SHA: exact and approved. bun audit: 1 moderate advisory (minimatch 10.2.6, GHSA-g3hv-75wg-m249) in the dev-only lint toolchain, exit 1 (note N5). Docker: not applicable, no Dockerfile. CI: ci.yml has permissions contents: read and calls pulse-config check.yml@51e95b0 (full SHA), which uses actions/checkout@3d3c42e (v7.0.1) with persist-credentials: false and oven-sh/setup-bun@0c5077e (v2.2.0), both approved, and checks dist is up to date; dist/ is unchanged after bun run build in the copy.

findings.title: Compressed responses get around the fetchJson 5 MiB body cap: the runtime decodes the whole body in memory first
findings.class: decompression bomb (resource exhaustion) that gets around a documented body limit
findings.command: A local server answers one GET with a brotli- or zstd-encoded body of a few KiB that decodes to 1-2 GiB; fetchJson with the default cap; peak RSS sampled in a fresh Bun process (SEC-1 expectation: peak RSS growth under 64 MiB)
findings.excerpt: SEC-1 kind=too-large peakRssDeltaMiB=1305 compressedBytes=1681 | fresh processes: brotli 2 KiB -> +1,336 MiB in 2.1 s; brotli 3 KiB -> +2,568 MiB in 4.3 s; zstd 32 KiB -> +2,056 MiB; gzip/deflate +178 MiB; plain endless body +13 MiB | body cancelled without a read: +1,330 MiB; Accept-Encoding identity: +1,330 MiB; Bun decompress:false: +2 MiB
findings.impact: One response of a few KiB makes every caller that passes Bun's fetch (probe check list, status api poll, notify incident feed) allocate memory up to the decoded size and get killed in a memory-limited container, also on non-2xx answers. The response can come from the api origin, from any origin a redirect leads to (finding -3), or from an on-path attacker on a plain-http api URL. The documented 5 MiB cap does not bound memory.
findings.fixDirection: Stop the runtime from decoding ahead of the cap: set Bun's decompress: false on the request init (other runtimes ignore it), then refuse a response whose Content-Encoding is not identity, or decode it in a streaming decoder inside the byte-counting loop that stops at maxBytes. Add a test with an encoded response.

findings.title: A header entry named __proto__ is never validated (zod record skips it, the input object is returned), and pulse-probe then loads no checks
findings.class: validation bypass through a reserved prototype key name
findings.command: A check parsed from JSON whose header record has an entry under the __proto__ key with a value of a wrong type; validateCheck and validateAdminCheckInput, then pulse-probe loadChecks (copy) with that check and one valid check (SEC-2 expectation)
findings.excerpt: SEC-2 validateCheck ok=true validateAdminCheckInput ok=true | values of a wrong type, a variable without the PULSE_HEADER_ prefix, CR/LF and an over-long value all pass; the entry does not count toward 20 headers or 16 KiB | probe: loadChecks throws TypeError (property read at src/client.ts:148), the valid check is not loaded either | zod 4.6.7 schemas.js:1762 skips the key; contract src/validate-core.ts:241-247 keeps it, :314 returns the input
findings.impact: A writer of checks (admin token, or the checks file; api src/config.ts:160 and :249 validate with validateCheck) can store one check that every probe fails to load: at startup it retries without end, a running probe keeps its old list. The probe re-checks env prefix and host binding, so no other environment variable is read.
findings.fixDirection: Reject an own __proto__ key in the header record in the contract (recordView or a check on the input), or validate every own entry value without zod's record loop; add tests for that key under each header rule.

findings.title: fetchJson follows redirects to other origins and from https to http, and forwards custom credential headers there
findings.command: Local origin answers 302/307 to another host name and port; a TLS origin answers 302 to plain http; fetchJson with a credential in a custom header (SEC-3 expectation)
findings.excerpt: SEC-3 crossOrigin ok=true httpsToHttp ok=true | 1 request at the redirect target each time, its body returned as value | x-api-key received by the other origin and the plain-http host; Authorization and Cookie dropped by Bun | notify sets redirect: manual itself (src/api.ts:137), probe and status do not
findings.impact: Whoever can make the api origin or a proxy in front of it answer with a redirect makes probe and status read their data from another host or over plain http, where it can be forged; custom credential headers cross to that host; it widens finding -1.
findings.fixDirection: Set redirect: "error" (or "manual" and treat 3xx as an http error) in the init that fetchJson builds, so every consumer gets it.

findings.title: The upstream x-pulse-contract header value appears unshortened in fetchJson errors (wire-mismatch message and http wire.error)
findings.class: upstream reply text in errors and logs
findings.command: Local server answers 200 and 500 with a long x-pulse-contract value that holds a marker; fetchJson (SEC-4 expectation)
findings.excerpt: SEC-4 kind=wire-mismatch errorLength=4089 upstreamTextInError=true | 8,014-character header -> 8,089-character error object | 500: {"kind":"http","status":500,"wire":{"status":"mismatch","error":"x-pulse-contract: got \"<marker>\", expected 1"}}
findings.impact: A header value from the api or a proxy, up to the runtime header limit, reaches every consumer log line that prints the error, unshortened and unescaped.
findings.fixDirection: Use a fixed text (x-pulse-contract: expected 1), or at most a short escaped prefix of the value.

findings.title: The fetchJson invalid-json error carries text from the upstream response body (the JSON.parse message)
findings.class: upstream reply text in errors and logs
findings.command: Local server answers 200 with a non-JSON body that has a bare word where the parser fails; fetchJson (SEC-5 expectation)
findings.excerpt: SEC-5 kind=invalid-json upstreamTextInError=true | message: JSON Parse error: Unexpected identifier "<upstream token>" | a token in a JSON-like value appears too | HTML body: only "Unrecognized token '<'"
findings.impact: A token from an upstream or proxy reply can reach the logs of probe, status and notify when the bare word comes first at the failing position. Root cause of notify finding security-notify-2026-10-31-2.
findings.fixDirection: Use a fixed message such as 'response is not valid JSON', as the http and too-large cases already do.

findings.title: Getters on Object.prototype run in schema refinements that read zod's output (audit, maintenance, manual incident, latency day), contrary to docs/index.md:359
findings.class: inherited accessor runs during validation (needs a poisoned runtime)
findings.command: Define a counting getter without setter on Object.prototype for one field name, validate a valid audit entry (SEC-6 expectation); same per field name over all 42 cases
findings.excerpt: SEC-6 getterRuns=1 validEntryOk=false | runs for start/end (5 each), action (2), status and resolvedAt (6 each), count/p50Ms/p95Ms (180 each) | Object.prototype numeric-index getter: 24 of the 42 validator cases reject valid input with 'is not a valid value' | also src/schema.ts:561, :689, :882, src/admin.ts:118, :132

notes: N1: an accessor on an optional field (31 cases) reads as absent and the result is ok:true with the same object returned; a later read by the caller runs the getter. A Proxy get trap can do the same (documented at src/validate-core.ts:288-292). Consumers validate JSON.parse output only.

N2: on a network error, fetchJson returns the raw runtime error as cause; in Bun 1.4.0 its path property holds the full URL with user info and query (JSON.stringify(cause) shows it, String(cause) does not).
N3: maxBytes NaN or Infinity turns the cap off (endless body: timeout after 2 s, RSS +1.4 GiB); a caller option, not untrusted input.
N4: errors repeat input key names (unknown keys, header names), not values, with no length limit.
N5: bun audit: minimatch 10.2.6 (moderate, GHSA-g3hv-75wg-m249), dev-only via pulse-config -> eslint.
N6: validation time near the 5 MiB cap is at most 279 ms over 6 shapes, 3 runs each; nothing is superlinear.
N7: a check url may target loopback, private or link-local addresses by design; the probe's src/address-policy.ts holds the target policy.
N8: getManualIncidents and getManualIncident drop the path of a base URL that has a query; a correctness note, not a security problem.
